title: What is Terraform? Infrastructure as code explained
seoTitle: What Is Terraform? Infrastructure as Code Guide
seoDescription: Learn how Terraform uses configuration, providers, state and plans to manage infrastructure as code, plus its benefits and trade-offs.
excerpt: Terraform turns infrastructure definitions into a reviewable workflow for creating and changing cloud and platform resources.
author: KitsuWire Editorial
keyTakeaways: Terraform is an infrastructure-as-code tool that manages resources through declarative configuration and provider APIs.
The plan workflow previews proposed changes before apply executes them.
Terraform state maps configuration to managed real-world resources and must be protected carefully.
Modules improve reuse, but good IaC still requires architecture, review, testing and lifecycle discipline.
body: Cloud platforms made infrastructure programmable. Terraform gives teams a common language and workflow for describing many of those resources as code rather than creating them manually in web consoles.
Terraform is declarative: configuration describes the desired infrastructure, and Terraform determines actions needed to move managed resources toward that state.

sections.heading: Configuration and providers
paragraphs: Terraform configurations are commonly written in HashiCorp Configuration Language. Resource blocks describe infrastructure objects and data sources read information that already exists.
Providers are plugins that connect Terraform to APIs such as cloud platforms, Kubernetes and SaaS systems. Each provider defines the resource types and attributes it can manage.

sections.heading: Init, plan and apply
paragraphs: terraform init prepares a working directory and installs required providers. terraform plan compares configuration, state and provider information to produce a proposed set of changes.
terraform apply executes an approved plan. Reviewing plans is one of Terraform's most important operational habits because infrastructure changes can be destructive or expensive.

sections.heading: Why Terraform needs state
paragraphs: Terraform state records information about managed resources and their relationship to configuration. Without that mapping, Terraform could not reliably determine what it already controls.

Teams commonly store state in a remote backend with access controls and locking. State can contain sensitive values, so it should be treated as protected operational data rather than a harmless cache.

sections.heading: Modules and reusable infrastructure
paragraphs: Modules package related Terraform configuration behind inputs and outputs. Organizations use modules to standardize networks, clusters, databases and other recurring patterns.
A useful module creates a stable abstraction. An overly complicated module can hide important behavior and become harder to evolve than straightforward configuration.

sections.heading: Drift and lifecycle management
paragraphs: Drift occurs when real infrastructure changes outside the expected Terraform workflow. Plans can reveal differences, but teams still need policies about whether to import, revert or accept external changes.
Infrastructure also has lifecycle constraints. Replacing a database is very different from replacing a stateless test VM, so plans must be interpreted in the context of the workload.

sections.heading: What Terraform does not solve
paragraphs: Terraform provisions resources but does not automatically design secure networks, choose good architectures or operate applications. It is one layer in a broader platform and delivery system.
Configuration management, application deployment, secrets management and policy tooling may complement Terraform depending on the environment.

faq.question: Is Terraform only for AWS?
faq.answer: No. Terraform has providers for many cloud platforms, Kubernetes, SaaS products and infrastructure systems.

faq.question: Why is Terraform state important?
faq.answer: State lets Terraform map configuration to real managed resources and calculate changes. Losing or exposing state can create operational and security problems.

faq.question: Is Terraform the same as Ansible?
faq.answer: No. Their capabilities can overlap, but Terraform is primarily focused on resource provisioning and lifecycle, while Ansible is widely used for configuration management and automation.
